page: Microsoft Azure EC16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor offering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector instructions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Resource allocation provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features a bundled local SSD pool measuring 644 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable for attached remote storage. The system includes zero GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on internal network configurations or attached IPs.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 3024.57, a Geekbench single-core score of 1953.0, and a Geekbench text processing score of 2528.0. Multi-core and throughput metrics operate firmly within the middle 50% tier, showing a stress-ng multi-core result of 24143.9, a PassMark CPU score of 25637.87, and Geekbench multi-core score of 10931.0. The memory subsystem recorded a PassMark memory score of 2521.3 and Redis SET operations reaching 20.5 million operations per second, with database operations scoring 7281.63.

Given its substantial 128.0 GB memory capacity paired with local high-speed SSD storage, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-caching tasks without the pricing overhead of GPU accelerators. Microsoft Azure EC16ads_v6 is structured primarily for relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, data processing pipelines, and general enterprise memory-optimized workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure EC16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for memory-dense tasks, it provides 128.0 GB of RAM alongside 644 GB of local SSD storage, while omitting GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks show upper-quartile single-core CPU execution, paired with median-range multi-core performance, recording 20.5 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a 25637.87 PassMark CPU score. Instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptography. The combination of an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and local temporary SSD makes this server well-suited for relational database deployments, in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing.
